papers.title: Who Remembers What? Multi-Granularity Memory Extraction for Multi-User, Multi-Agent Interaction
papers.problem: Agents that share lessons across many users and agents can leak one person's private facts.
papers.fix: MixUA scopes each lesson, lifts pass rates up to 16 points, and leaks at most 0.02% of private probes.
papers.practicalUseCase: Shared agent memory can help everyone without leaking secrets, so label each stored lesson with who may read it.
papers.limitation: Tests used only five users and seven agents on a purpose-built benchmark.

papers.title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming
papers.problem: Robots struggle to learn from human, robot, and simulated demonstrations because bodies, sensors, and controls differ.
papers.fix: EgoX pretraining on mixed demonstrations raises average task progress from 0.63 to 0.80 across 13 task-robot pairs.
papers.practicalUseCase: Robots can borrow skill from human and simulated data, so mix many data sources before training one robot.
papers.limitation: Results cover five tasks and six robot bodies, including five physical robots and one simulated humanoid.

papers.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
papers.problem: Video models compress frames into small codes, which limits resolution, frame-level control, and quick response to each action.
papers.fix: PixVid draws video in pixels, stays competitive with the latent baseline, and doubles resolution at equal token count.
papers.practicalUseCase: Pixel-space video can respond at the next frame, so watch for more interactive video tools.
papers.limitation: It tests one base model, Wan2.1-14B, fine-tuned on about 1.3M clips.

papers.title: Consensus Capture in Reference-Based UAV Video Stabilization: A Benchmark on Dynamic Urban Scenes
papers.problem: Drone video stabilizers are tested on scenes where only the camera moves, so moving traffic can pull them off.
papers.fix: Unmasked ORB followed moving vehicles on 28 of 304 real-time pairs, and masking removed this error for every method.
papers.practicalUseCase: Usual quality counts miss this error, so mask moving objects before stabilizing busy-street video.
papers.limitation: Tests cover hovering drones over urban intersections, so other scenes may behave differently.

papers.title: Sharīʿah Compliance in Malaysia’s Digital Payment Systems: Evidence from Expert Interviews
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.leadAuthor: Wan Anis Wan Mohd Assrudin et al.
papers.problem: Malaysia has digital payment rules, but experts still doubt that providers follow Islamic law in practice.
papers.fix: Ten Islamic law experts say doubts remain, mainly about non-bank payment providers with less established governance.
papers.practicalUseCase: Non-bank payment apps may carry more Islamic-law risk, so check who oversees their compliance before using one.
papers.limitation: It covers only Malaysia and ten interviewed experts, so it shows views, not measured compliance.

papers.title: Interest Prohibitions and Contract Design in Medieval Christianity and Islam
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: Interest bans in medieval Europe and Islamic law left open how lenders could still earn a return.
papers.fix: European lenders built return into indirect contracts, while Islamic law tied return to trade, partnership, and shared risk.
papers.practicalUseCase: Contract form decides whether a deal counts as lawful return, so check ownership transfer, documents, and who bears loss.
papers.limitation: It reviews old texts and secondary history, with no new archive data or prevalence estimates.

papers.title: Financial Depth and Stability in Dual Banking Systems
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: Studies lacked multi-country evidence on whether Islamic finance alongside conventional banks helps a national economy grow.
papers.fix: In 27 countries over 2010 to 2024, higher Islamic finance share linked to more private credit and faster growth.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, policymakers can back dual banking and add Islamic small-business credit lines beside conventional ones.
papers.limitation: It studies only dual-banking countries and omits countries with a single system, because global data are limited.

papers.title: “The significance of context”: Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD
papers.problem: Little data shows how adults with ADHD fare building a career in academia.
papers.fix: Early-career academics with ADHD say academia can reward them, but social and institutional pressure often blocks it.
papers.practicalUseCase: Work context shapes ADHD outcomes, so choose or shape workplaces that fit how you think.
papers.limitation: It is a qualitative interview study of early-career academics, so it shows experiences, not how common they are.

papers.title: Procrastination among US college students: Prevalence and impact relative to common health and life issues
papers.problem: It was unclear how common student procrastination is and how it ranks against other student problems.
papers.fix: Of 65,950 US students, 72.3% reported procrastination, and 45.4% said it hurt grades, most among 36 issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Procrastination hurts grades 2.8 to 3.5 times more often than money or ADHD issues, so tackle it first.
papers.limitation: It uses self-reports from US college students, so it shows links, not cause.
